newsitem.title: GERMANY: German cartel offices expands price fixing probe.
newsitem.headline: German cartel offices expands price fixing probe.

text.p: Germany's cartel office on Monday widened a price-fixing probe in the power cable industry to include several more groups after having charged five firms with wrongdoing and issuing a hefty fine.
The cartel office said additional firms have been charged with cooperating with competitors to divide up the market amongst themselves, thereby influencing prices for high-voltage power cables.
A cartel office spokeswoman, however, declined to identify the additional firms, saying not all of the companies have been notified.

The office had so far identified electronics giants Siemens AG, Alcatel subsidiaries Kabel Rheydt and Kabelmetal Electro, Felten & Guilleaume as well as ABB to have participated in the price-fixing scheme.

German television station N-TV reported that Alcatel would be forced to pay 100 million marks ($60 million), the lion's share of the 260 million mark total, which would be the highest fine ever imposed by the German cartel office.
Siemens is expected to pay 90 million marks, the station reported.

The cartel office declined to officially confirm the groups would be fined 260 million marks. Spokesmen at Alcatel and Siemens also refused to comment on the issue, as they had not yet received appropriate documents from Berlin.
